recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes the remaining build-scope mismatch without adding redundant narrative or reopening later FHIR-45479 wording.
issue_request: FHIR-19602 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to clarify that OID, UUID, and URI-valued identifiers use urn:ietf:rfc:3986 only when no more specific identifier system has been assigned, with DICOM UID as the motivating example.
initial_application: Commit b7c51c4130 applied GF#19602 by adding the datatypes.html clarification and changing DICOM examples to use urn:dicom:uid with plain UID values. Later FHIR-45479 edits refactored the narrative into the current assigned-system/fallback wording, but the active Identifier spreadsheet still had a blanket Identifier.value comment requiring urn:ietf:rfc:3986 for any full URI value.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Identifier as an active datatype, so source/datatypes/identifier.xml is current build-scope source. The original Zulip discussion and later FHIR-45479 discussion support the same interpretation: specific identifier systems can be used for globally unique OID/UUID/URI-shaped values, and urn:ietf:rfc:3986 is the fallback when no identifier system has been assigned.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/identifier.xml so the Identifier.value detailed comment says Identifier.system SHALL identify the assigned identifier system for a globally unique identifier expressed as a URI, and SHALL be urn:ietf:rfc:3986 only when no identifier system has been assigned.
source_changes: source/datatypes/identifier.xml: replaced the stale Identifier.value comment that forced all full URI values to urn:ietf:rfc:3986 with wording that allows assigned identifier systems and uses urn:ietf:rfc:3986 only as the no-assigned-system fallback.
